newsitem.title: USA: Fleming earnings rise despite lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Fleming earnings rise despite lower sales.

text.p: Fleming Cos. Inc. Thursday said its fourth-quarter earnings rose despite lower sales, citing effective expense controls and cost reductions.
Fleming, the Oklahoma City-based supermarket owner and food distributor, said earnings were also aided by improved operating results in the retail food segment and lower equity investment losses.

For the quarter, Fleming earned $10.3 million, or 27 cents a share, compared with $4.0 million, or 11 cents a share a year earlier. Revenues declined to $3.87 billion from $4.14 billion a year earlier.

"Carefully managed margin improvements and expense controls helped drive performance gains in 1996 despite sales shortfalls in our food distribution operations," said Chief Executive Officer Robert E. Stauth.

"Fleming also took steps to strengthen earnings from our retail food operations. We divested 62 non-strategic stores and invested in four new stores. We also completed 41 remodels and made several major retail systems improvements in 1996," he said in a statement.
Fleming's 1997 plans call for 13 new stores and at least 20 remodels.
Currently, Fleming serves more than 3,100 supermarkets and operates approximately 270 company-owned stores.
For the year, Fleming earned $26.7 million, or 71 cents a share, compared with $42 million, or $1.12 a share a year earlier.
Sales declined to $16.49 billion from $17.50 billion a year earlier.
Fleming stock was up 12.5 cents at $16.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
